My sister stayed at Illickal PG girls hostel, and honestly, it turned out to be more than just a place to stay—it felt like a second home for her.

What stood out the most wasn’t just the clean rooms or the decent food (which, by the way, she said was simple but satisfying), but the kind of care and attention she received there. At one point, she fell sick while staying there, and that’s when we truly saw the difference. The staff didn’t just “check in” on her—they genuinely took responsibility. They made sure she was comfortable, took her to the hospital, and stayed supportive throughout.

And I have to specifically mention the owner aunty. My sister couldn’t stop talking about how kind and attentive she was. She treated her like her own daughter, constantly checking on her, making sure she was eating properly, and just being there in a way that’s rare to find these days. As someone who wasn’t physically there, knowing my sister had someone like that around gave me a lot of peace of mind.

Overall, the place is clean, safe, and well-maintained—but more importantly, it has heart. It’s not just a hostel; it’s a place where someone actually cares about you. As a former resident, I faced several issues that prospective students should know about:

1. Unfair Curfew Policy
This is the only boys' hostel in CUSAT with a strict curfew. Once, my train from Calicut was delayed by several hours, and I reached Ernakulam around 10:30 PM. Despite explaining the situation, the warden refused to open the gate and even shouted that I should have started my journey in the morning. I was forced to stay in a hotel that night. When my parents later questioned the management, they simply apologized and avoided responsibility. Ironically, the gate has been opened for others arriving at much later hours, which makes the policy seem inconsistent and selective.

2. Excessive Electricity Charges
Even though the hostel rooftop is fully covered with solar panels, separate electricity meters are maintained for each room and students are charged around ₹11 per unit, which is unusually high. My roommate and I only used two lights, one fan, and charged our phones, yet we regularly received bills of around ₹600. When we questioned the ₹11/unit rate, the management claimed that they themselves pay that amount to KSEB and that the same rate has been charged since around 2012. No clear justification or breakdown was provided.

3. Poor Cleanliness
The common bathrooms are often unhygienic and remain uncleaned for 3–4 days at a time, despite assurances during admission that cleaning would be done daily.

4. Delay in Returning Caution Deposit
At the time of admission, students are told that the caution deposit will be returned within 2–3 days after checkout. In reality, getting the refund often requires repeated calls and follow-ups, with the usual response being that there are too many students to process.

Many first-year students end up choosing this hostel without knowing these realities.
